# coderforge_machine (Data Source)

Look up a machine that exists in Cloud Builder, whether or not Terraform manages it. Useful for pointing a network rule at a machine someone else created.

The generated password is not available here: Cloud Builder returns it only at creation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look up a machine someone else created, to point a rule at it.
data "coderforge_machine" "legacy_db" {
  name = "db-legacy"
}

resource "coderforge_network_rule" "postgres" {
  src_port  = "15432"
  dest_ip   = data.coderforge_machine.legacy_db.ip
  dest_port = "5432"
}

output "legacy_db_state" {
  value = data.coderforge_machine.legacy_db.state
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the machine to look up.

### Read-Only

- `cpu` (Number) Virtual CPU count.
- `desired_state` (String) Power state the machine currently satisfies.
- `id` (String) Same as `name`.
- `ip` (String) Assigned address, if any.
- `managed_by` (String) Owning resource, if any.
- `message` (String)
- `network` (String) Configured network adapters.
- `ram` (Number) Memory in MiB.
- `raw_status` (String) Hypervisor status verbatim.
- `rid` (String) Cloud Builder resource id.
- `state` (String) Normalised state.
- `username` (String) Default account.
